dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5701.text: Hair on the cheeks or temples. Formed from 髟, with 賓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5702.text: Long hair. Formed from 髟, with 㒼 indicating the sound. Read like 蔓.

shuowen:5703.text: Long hair. Formed from 髟, with 監 indicating the sound. Read like 濫 in the Spring and Autumn’s “Heigong fled here with Lan.”

shuowen:5704.text: Beautiful hair. Formed from 髟 and 差.

shuowen:5705.text: Beautiful hair. Formed from 髟, with 卷 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “That man is handsome and has lovely hair.”

shuowen:5706.text: Hair. Formed from 髟 and 毛.

shuowen:5707.text: The appearance of hair. Formed from 髟, with 臱 indicating the sound. Read like 宀.

shuowen:5708.text: Abundant hair. Formed from 髟, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5709.text: The appearance of hair. Formed from 髟, with 爾 indicating the sound. Read like 𩯨, the term south of the Yangtze for vinegar starter.

shuowen:5710.text: The appearance of hair. Formed from 髟, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5711.text: Hair reaching the eyebrows. Formed from 髟, with 敄 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Hanging are those two locks.”

shuowen:5712.text: The appearance of a woman’s temple hair hanging down. Formed from 髟, with 前 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5713.text: Drooping temple hair, 鬋. Another explanation: a long appearance. Formed from 髟, with 兼 indicating the sound. Read like 慊.

shuowen:5714.text: A small amount of bound hair. Formed from 髟, with 截 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5715.text: A hairpiece, 髲. Formed from 髟, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5716.text: A hairpiece, 鬄. Formed from 髟, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5717.text: To use coarse and fine combs. Formed from 髟, with 次 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5718.text: To bind or arrange the hair neatly. Formed from 髟, with 𠯑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5719.text: A hair knot lying flat. Formed from 髟, with 般 indicating the sound. Read like 槃.

shuowen:5720.text: To tie or knot. Formed from 髟, with 付 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5721.text: A knotted headband ornament. Formed from 髟, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5722.text: Coiled hair. Formed from 髟, with 貴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5723.text: To fasten a hair knot with a pin. Formed from 髟, with 介 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5724.text: Hair standing or flowing, 鬣鬣. Formed from 髟, with 巤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5725.text: A mane. Formed from 髟, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5726.text: 髴 means seeming or resembling. Formed from 髟, with 弗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5727.text: Disordered hair. Formed from 髟, with abbreviated 茸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5728.text: Hair falling down. Formed from 髟 and abbreviated 隋.

shuowen:5729.text: Temple hair and head hair. Formed from 髟, with 春 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5730.text: Bald at the temples. Formed from 髟, with 閒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5731.text: To shave the hair. Formed from 髟 and 刀, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5732.text: To shave the hair. Formed from 髟, with 兀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5733.text: To shave the hair. Formed from 髟, with 弟 indicating the sound. For adults it is 髡, for children 鬀; shaving all the body hair as well is 𩮜.

shuowen:5734.text: A sudden apparition, 䰁. Formed from 髟, with 竝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5735.text: 𩮗, to appear suddenly. Formed from 髟, with 录 indicating the sound. 录 is large-seal 魅, also conveying sudden appearance.

shuowen:5736.text: A mourning hair knot. The Rites prescribes: women bind their hair for mourning, but do not do so merely when offering condolences. When Zang Wuzhong of Lu fought Qi at Hutai, Lu people receiving the dead first bound their hair this way. Formed from 髟, with 坐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5737.text: A horse’s mane. Formed from 髟, with 耆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5738.text: A small child’s hanging hair knot. Formed from 髟, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5739.text: To gather the hair. Formed from 髟, with 吉 indicating the sound. Ancient writing also uses 結.

shuowen:5740.text: To gather the hair. Formed from 髟, with 睘 indicating the sound. Note: ancient women’s head ornaments consisted of two carved jade rings. This and the preceding graph were both added by later people.

shuowen:5741.text: A ruler succeeding to the throne. Depicts a person issuing commands to the four quarters, hence 厂. Formed from 一 and 口: the one issuing commands is the ruler. All characters in this group follow 后.

shuowen:5742.text: A deep sound of anger. Formed from 口 and 后; 后 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5743.text: A minister administering affairs outside. Formed from reversed 后. All characters in this group follow 司.

shuowen:5744.text: Intention within, words expressed outwardly. Formed from 司 and 言.

shuowen:5745.text: A round vessel, also called 觛, for regulating eating and drinking. Depicts a person with 卪 below. The Changes says: “The gentleman regulates food and drink.” All characters in the 巵 group follow 巵.

shuowen:5746.text: A small 巵 cup with handles and a lid. Formed from 巵, with 專 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5747.text: A small 巵 cup. Formed from 巵, with 耑 indicating the sound. Read like 捶 in 捶擊.

shuowen:5748.text: A credential of authority. State guardians use jade tallies; guardians of towns and border districts, horn tallies; envoys to mountain states, tiger tallies; those to 士邦 states, human tallies; those to marsh states, dragon tallies; gate and pass officials, matching tallies; trade, seal tallies; roads, banner tallies. Depicts matching halves. All characters in the 卪 group follow 卪. The category 士邦 is uncertain.

shuowen:5749.text: To issue commands. Formed from 亼 and 卪.

shuowen:5750.text: To assist faithfully. Formed from 卪, with 比 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Assist in completing the five zones.”

shuowen:5751.text: To have great breadth of mind. Formed from 卪, with 多 indicating the sound. Read like 侈.

shuowen:5752.text: To administer it. Formed from 卪, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5753.text: High. Formed from 卪, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5754.text: 科厄, a knot in wood. Formed from 卪, with 厂 indicating the sound. Attendant Jia explains 厄 as wrapping. Another explanation: covering.

shuowen:5755.text: The joint at the head of the shin. Formed from 卪, with 桼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5756.text: The knee bent. Formed from 卪, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5757.text: To restrain desire. Formed from 卪, with 谷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5758.text: To leave the carriage and unhitch the horses. Formed from 卪, 止 and 午. Read like 寫 in the Runan pronunciation of 寫書.

shuowen:5759.text: Two 卪. 巽 follows this element. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:5760.text: A tally or joint, 卪. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:5761.text: The credential held by those exercising authority. Formed from 爪 and 卪. All characters in this group follow 印.

shuowen:5762.text: To press. Formed from reversed 印.

shuowen:5763.text: The expression or complexion of the face. Formed from 人 and 卪. All characters in this group follow 色.

shuowen:5764.text: The face showing an agitated expression. Formed from 色, with 弗 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “His expression was agitated.”

shuowen:5765.text: A pale blue color. Formed from 色, with 并 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5766.text: The regulation of affairs. Formed from 卩 and 㔿. All characters in this group follow 𠨍. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:5767.text: To make manifest. The six ministers are the Celestial Office’s Chief Steward, Earth Office’s Minister of Education, Spring Office’s Chief of Rites, Summer Office’s Minister of War, Autumn Office’s Minister of Justice and Winter Office’s Minister of Works. Formed from 𠨍, with 皀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5768.text: Law. Formed from 卩 and 辛, regulating crimes, and 口, representing the one applying the law. All characters in this group follow 辟.

shuowen:5769.text: To govern. Formed from 辟 and 井. The Book of Zhou says: “That I do not govern.”

shuowen:5770.text: To govern. Formed from 辟, with 乂 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Is there someone who can bring order?”

shuowen:5771.text: To wrap. Depicts a bent person enclosing something. All characters in this group follow 勹.

shuowen:5772.text: A curved spine. Formed from 勹, with abbreviated 𥷚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5773.text: To move on the hands. Formed from 勹, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5774.text: To lie prostrate on the ground. Formed from 勹, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5775.text: What is held in the hand is 匊. Formed from 勹 and 米.

shuowen:5776.text: Few or little. Formed from 勹 and 二.

shuowen:5777.text: To gather. Formed from 勹, with 九 indicating the sound. Read like 鳩.

shuowen:5778.text: A complete circuit. Ten days make a 旬. Formed from 勹 and 日.

shuowen:5779.text: To cover. Formed from 勹 covering 人.

shuowen:5780.text: A sound. Formed from 勹, with 凶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5781.text: To encompass all around. Formed from 勹, with 舟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5782.text: To surround. Formed from 勹 and 合; 合 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5783.text: Sated. Formed from 勹, with 㲃 indicating the sound. At popular sacrifices, the invoker says: “Be fully sated.”

shuowen:5784.text: Repeated or doubled. Formed from 勹, with 復 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5785.text: A high burial mound. Formed from 勹, with 豖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5786.text: Depicts a pregnant person, with 巳 inside representing a child not yet fully formed. Primal qi begins at 子; a child is what people produce. The male moves leftward for thirty, the female rightward for twenty; both stand at 巳 and become husband and wife. Pregnancy begins at 巳; 巳 becomes 子, and birth occurs after ten months. The male starts at 巳 and reaches 寅; the female starts at 巳 and reaches 申. Hence male years begin at 寅, female years at 申. All characters in this group follow 包.

shuowen:5787.text: The wrapping in which a child is born. Formed from 肉 and 包.

shuowen:5788.text: A bottle gourd. Formed from 包, with 夸 indicating the sound. 包 is used because it can contain things.

shuowen:5789.text: To urge and admonish oneself urgently. Formed from abbreviated 羊 and abbreviated 包, together with 口, conveying caution in speech. 羊 uses the same principle as 義, 善 and 美. All characters in this group follow 茍.

shuowen:5790.text: Reverent. Formed from 攴 and 茍.

shuowen:5791.text: What people return to becomes 鬼. Formed from 人, depicting a ghost’s head. Ghosts’ yin qi harms, hence 厶. All characters in this group follow 鬼.

shuowen:5792.text: A spirit. Formed from 鬼, with 申 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5793.text: Yang qi. Formed from 鬼, with 云 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5794.text: A yin spirit. Formed from 鬼, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5795.text: A malevolent ghost. Formed from 鬼, with 失 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5796.text: A spirit causing depletion. Formed from 鬼, with 虚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5797.text: A drought demon. Formed from 鬼, with 犮 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou has the Red Ba officer, who removes creatures from walls and roofs. The Odes says: “The drought demon wreaks havoc.”

shuowen:5798.text: An old thing that has become a spirit. Formed from 鬼 and 彡; 彡 represents a ghost’s hair.

shuowen:5799.text: A ghost’s clothing. Another explanation: a child ghost. Formed from 鬼, with 支 indicating the sound. The Han Odes Commentary says: “Zheng Jiaofu met two women wearing ghostly garments.”

shuowen:5800.text: A ghost’s appearance. Formed from 鬼, with 虎 indicating the sound.
